text:
The court will likely overrule the objections and admit the records, because the defendant's testimony that he kept them on a regular business basis can serve as the qualified-witness foundation under FRE 803(6) and as authentication under FRE 901. I'm revising my earlier answer, which treated that testimony as too conclusory when the rules require only a witness familiar with the record-keeping practice, not a detailed explanation. The "defendant is available" rationale is wrong, because a declarant's availability doesn't remove hearsay status for his own out-of-court statements offered by him.

CONFIDENCE: 65
